page: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-88-lssd is a general-purpose virtual machine optimized for high-throughput computation and fast I/O workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor clocked at 2.7 GHz, the instance delivers 88 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 44 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It features 105 MB of L3 cache alongside hardware support for vector and matrix extensions such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions). Complementing the processor is 352 GB of system RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per vCPU. No dedicated accelerators or GPUs are included.

A primary architectural feature of the c3-standard-88-lssd is its integrated local storage array. The server includes 6,432 GB of local NVMe SSD storage across 16 drives, providing ultra-low-latency scratch space and high data throughput directly attached to the host. Networking configurations do not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on private networking or separately configured network routing.

Benchmark results highlight top-tier and strong throughput across parallel workloads. In multi-core assessments, it achieved 73,268.7 in stress-ng and 18,439.0 in Geekbench multi-core tests, placing it in the top quartile of evaluated instances. The server demonstrates top-tier capability in Geekbench image processing (18,891.0) and strong performance in Clang software compilation (50,178.0) and ray tracing (85,655.0). Memory bandwidth reaches 224.79 GB/sec for large uncached read blocks and 99.15 GB/sec for uncached writes. Conversely, single-thread metrics—such as a single-core Geekbench score of 1,724.0 and gzip compression at 26.3 GB/sec—remain in the middle 50% baseline.

From an operational and workload perspective, the server offers high resource density for high-concurrency tasks. It achieves strong throughput in in-memory and database scenarios, recording 85.97 million Redis SET operations per second and 29,774.57 in PassMark database operations. In CPU-based inference workloads, the AMX-capable Xeon cores provide robust prompt processing, delivering 3,879.32 tokens/sec on small 135M models and 222.51 tokens/sec on 7B models. The combination of dense multi-core processing, substantial RAM, and fast local NVMe capacity makes the instance suitable for large-scale relational or NoSQL databases, distributed caching, heavy CI/CD build farms, and high-throughput static web serving.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-88-lssd is a general-purpose instance featuring 88 dedicated vCPUs (44 physical cores) based on the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8481C architecture at 2.7 GHz, paired with 352 GB of RAM and 6,432 GB of local NVMe SSD storage across 16 drives. Built without dedicated GPUs, it includes instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX. In benchmarks, the server demonstrates strong multi-core performance, recording 18,439.0 on Geekbench multi-core and 73,268.7 on stress-ng, accompanied by 85.97 million operations per second on Redis SET tests and top-tier Geekbench image processing. Single-core performance falls within average ranges. With its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation and high-throughput local disk storage, the c3-standard-88-lssd is engineered for high-concurrency workloads, including distributed databases, intensive software compilation pipelines, in-memory caching systems, and containerized microservices requiring rapid local I/O.
